Optimal.Notes: A solid balance of visual quality and battery life — medium textures and shadows look good on the Deck screen while the 40 Hz lock keeps gameplay smooth and eliminates screen tearing. Ambient Occlusion is disabled as it costs disproportionate GPU time.

profiles.Summary: XCOM 2 runs well on the Steam Deck via Proton, benefiting from its native Linux port (via Feral Interactive) and relatively modest GPU requirements that the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU handles comfortably. The game is turn-based so frame rate consistency matters more than raw numbers, and 40–60 fps is achievable at medium-to-high settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC system requirements (the Deck's GPU is comfortably above the minimum and close to the recommended spec) and the game's 2016 vintage. On first run, check fps during a busy combat turn with many soldiers and explosions — if it dips below your cap, lower Shadow Quality first, then Effects Quality.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 upscaled via FSR to keep the GPU very light. Since XCOM 2 is turn-based, 30 fps is perfectly comfortable and the low TDP significantly extends session length.

KnownIssues: Long turn processing times (AI thinking) can cause brief frame dips that are unrelated to GPU settings.
Some UI text and menus may appear small at 1280x800 without scaling adjustments.
Occasional long loading times between missions have been reported on Deck.
The game may default to a windowed or incorrect resolution on first launch — verify display settings before playing.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at high settings is within reach for this 2016 title; expect occasional dips to the high 40s during explosive combat animations. Screen Space Reflections is kept off as it offers little visual benefit at the cost of notable GPU overhead.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz/40 fps is the sweet spot for XCOM 2 on Deck — the turn-based nature makes this feel perfectly smooth, and medium textures keep the tactical maps looking sharp. Ambient Occlusion and Depth of Field are disabled as they cost more than they're worth at this resolution.

profiles.Summary: XCOM 2 runs well on the Steam Deck via Proton (ProtonDB trending platinum), with the turn-based strategy gameplay being a natural fit for the hardware's controls and screen. The RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeds the game's minimum requirements, allowing for medium-to-high settings at native resolution with solid frame rates.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's 2016 PC requirements (which the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeds) and its ProtonDB gold/platinum trending status. On first run, check frame pacing during large tactical battles with many units and VFX — if you see dips below 40 fps on the Optimal profile, drop to Max Battery settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load minimal; turn-based pacing means the 30 fps cap is barely noticeable. TDP cap of 7 W is sufficient for this genre's workload.

KnownIssues: Long turn processing and end-of-turn animations can cause brief frame dips regardless of settings.
Some users report occasional stutters on the Geoscape/strategy layer, likely due to shader compilation.
The game's default controller layout may need adjustment — verify Steam Input layout before playing.
DLC/mod content from Steam Workshop may increase load times noticeably on the Deck's storage.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with high settings, XCOM 2 runs well within the Deck's capabilities given its age and modest PC requirements; expect 55-60 fps on most tactical maps with occasional dips during large explosions or complex animations. Full TDP is unlocked to let the APU boost freely.
